overview.description: Jhyap Yaniv (also known as Dhumbal in Nepal and Yaniv in Israel) is a unique draw-and-discard game. Unlike standard Rummy, the goal is to reduce your hand's point total to a minimum (typically 5 or 7) and then call 'Jhyap' (or 'Yaniv') to end the round. If another player has an equal or lower total, the caller is penalized, creating a tense game of memory and risk management.

history.origins: Originating in Nepal as 'Jhyap' or 'Dhumbal', the game was brought to Israel by backpackers in the late 1990s. In Israel, it was renamed 'Yaniv' after a traveler who allegedly standardized the rules. It has since become a global phenomenon among travelers.
timeline: 20th Century: Played in Nepal under various local names.
1990s: Israeli travelers bring the game home from the Himalayas.
2000s: Becomes a staple social game in Israel and Europe.
Present: Popular online and in traveler hostels worldwide.
history.evolution: The game's rules for 'Asaf' (losing a call) and the specific point values for Jacks/Queens/Kings vary between the original Nepali version and the modern Israeli version.
history.cultural: 'Jhyap' is Nepali slang for being 'high' or 'inebriated', reflecting the game's social and relaxed nature.

setup.deck: Standard 52-card deck + 2 Jokers. Aces = 1, Numbers = face value, Face cards = 10, Jokers = 0.
setup.dealing: Deal 5 cards to each player. Place the rest in a draw pile with one card turned up.

rules.objective: Have the lowest total points in hand and call 'Jhyap' to end the round.
rules.gameplay:
1. **Discard**: You may discard a single card, a set (2+ same rank), or a sequence (3+ same suit).
2. **Draw**: After discarding, you MUST draw one card from the draw pile OR the card discarded by the previous player.
3. **The Call**: At the start of your turn, if your total is 7 (or 5, depending on house rules) or less, you may shout 'Jhyap!'. Play stops immediately.
keyRules: Follow the legal action constraints defined for Jhyap Yaniv.
Round outcome is resolved by the scoring method: - If the caller has the lowest hand: They score 0 pts.
Winning condition: Have the lowest total points in hand and call 'Jhyap' to end the round.

strategy.basic: Always discard sets and sequences together to reduce your hand size quickly. Try to hold low cards like Aces and 2s for the endgame.
strategy.intermediate: Memorize the cards discarded by others. If your opponent just picked up a 2 from the discard pile, their hand is likely getting very lowâ€”don't wait too long to call.
strategy.advanced: The 'Wait-Exclusion': Sometimes it's better to wait an extra turn with 6 points if you suspect someone else has 5 or less. Let them call first and catch them in an Asaf.
tips: Jokers are goldâ€”worth 0 points, they are the best defense against a high score.
Don't pick up a high card from the discard pile unless it completes a sequence you can discard immediately.

list.name: Speedy Yaniv / Yan
list.description: Three cards each; half deck (two suits, one joker) for four or fewer players; call Yan at 5 or fewer points; 30-point penalty for calling Yaniv instead of Yan.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Variation changes hand size and call name only; no engine constant overrides.

list.name: Call limit
list.description: Agreed limit for calling Yaniv: 5, 6, 7, 10, 11, or 13 points; higher limits speed up the game. Some play with no limit but round cannot end before everyone has had one turn.

list.name: Nepal vs Israel scoring
list.description: Nepal: wrong-call penalty 25; others do not score hand points; 100-point elimination; no score reduction at 50/100. Israel: 30 penalty; 200 elimination; score reduced at 50/100/200 (or halved at 100/150/200).
list.emptyOverridesReason: Scoring and elimination differ by region; no single engine override.

discard.description: Throw one card, one set of two or more same rank, or one sequence of three or more same suit to the dump pile.
discard.constraints: At start of turn; one combination per turn; then must draw one card. Sequences in order; aces low.

go_out.description: Call Yaniv or Jhyap to end the round when your hand total is at or below the agreed limit (typically 5) and you believe you have the lowest total. Round ends; all reveal hands; caller scores 0 if lowest, or hand total plus 30 penalty if another has equal or lower (Asaf).
go_out.constraints: Only at start of your turn, before discarding; hand total must be at or below agreed limit (e.g. 5 or 6).

drawSources.notes: Only first or last card of previous player's set or sequence.

validPlays.notes: Single card, set of same rank, or sequence of three or more same suit; aces low in sequences.

shedding.burnRules: Discard before draw; one combination per turn (single card, set of same rank, or sequence same suit).

engine.deckDescription: One standard 52-card pack plus two jokers; five cards each; draw-and-discard; call Yaniv when you have the lowest hand total (Pagat).
engine.suitDescription: Four French suits (hearts, diamonds, clubs, spades); runs must be same suit; jokers wild; card values used for hand total and penalties.
engine.rankDescription: Standard ranks; number cards count face value, face cards typically 10; aces 1 or 11; aim for lowest total when calling Yaniv.
